explain.say: Put a pencil in a glass of water. It looks snapped in half! The pencil is fine, so what is going on? Light is bending as it moves between water and air. This bending is called refraction. Let us find out why it happens.

faq.q: Why does light slow down in glass?
faq.a: Light interacts with the atoms in glass, so it travels more slowly, about 200 000 kilometres per second instead of 300 000.
asks: How fast is light in glass?

faq.q: Why does light only bend at an angle?
faq.a: At an angle, one side of the beam slows before the other, so it swings round. Straight on, both sides slow together, so it does not bend.
asks: Does light bend if it hits straight on?

faq.a: The normal is an imaginary line drawn at right angles to the surface where the light hits. Angles are measured from it.
asks: What is the normal in refraction?

faq.a: Refraction is the change in direction of light when it passes from one material into another, because its speed changes.

faq.q: Why does a straw look bent in water?
faq.a: Light from the straw bends as it leaves the water into the air, so your eye sees the underwater part in the wrong place.
asks: Why does a pencil look broken in water?

facts: Light travels at about 300 000 km/s in air and about 200 000 km/s in glass.
Light entering a denser material bends towards the normal.
